column1: # behaviour.csv · teach-pendant · robot teach pendant (our own design; printed SIMULATION ONLY. NOT A SAFETY DEVICE: spec.md What; OPERATING.md 6; lib/behaviour.md). Written by elec-r30 (unattended; 2026-11-11) from spec.md (What; Dimensions; Named nodes; Decals; Notes) and element.py.

# No pin rows: the pendant cable to robot-controller and its gland are not built (spec.md Notes); the pendant has no terminal mark on file and no port node (element.py: the pivots are screen; estop; key-1 … key-16; enable). The cable's pins come with the cable in a later version and the pin rows with them; so no contact / load / source rows: what the E-stop and the enabling bar switch is not on file and not claimed (spec.md What: simulation inputs to the twin; never a safety function). EM's Safety sign-off at 1.0 (lib/approvals.csv row 37) stands on that label; this file makes no safety claim.

# Every state is the operator's: the E-stop a latch (press 6 and latch: spec.md Dimensions E-stop; toolkit/std22.py ESTOP) cleared by its own reset (the head twisted free); each key momentary (design: a key returns when released); the enabling bar momentary at its two pressed positions (enabled about 0.75; pressed through 1.5: spec.md Dimensions enabling bar); the screen lit while the twin sets the supply by hand (the cable is not built: a stand-in until its pins are on file).

# Key legends (J1− … J6+ and F1 … F4) are decals (spec.md Decals); which key carries which is the decal's and is not read here. Keys are numbered left to right and top row first (spec.md Named nodes): columns x −75 / −25 / 25 / 75 and rows z 5 / −21 / −47 / −73 (spec.md Dimensions keys).
